clue.text: Unexpectedly published, ring fellow livid about article

indicators.note: about here means positioned next to, the article standing beside the colour

parts.note: a book that is out has been published
a ring is round, like the letter O
the is the definite article
livid skin is bruised blue

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a published report about a jealous ring of men furious over an article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' merely places the article beside the colour word rather than containing it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for something arriving like lightning from a clear sky means it was entirely unforeseen.

clue.text: Rings about fabulous bird outside in river

indicators.note: about means the two ring letters wrap around everything else

parts.note: each ring is round like the letter O, two of them

indicators.note: outside means the bird's letters are placed around the little word in

parts.note: the roc is a giant mythical bird of Arabian tales
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rings are fixed to a mythical bird that lives beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' and 'about' are two nested containers: the bird wraps the little word, then the pair of rings wraps the lot, ending on the familiar South American name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orinoco is a major South American waterway flowing through Venezuela.

clue.text: Name in headline?

definitions.meaning: a name of a book or film, or a person's rank such as Sir
the heading over a newspaper article or chapter

explanation.definitionFit: Both a designation of a work and the heading over a piece are this word.

clue.text: To begin with, keep hugging a celebrity

indicators.note: hugging means the stronghold word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a keep is a castle's stronghold, a fort
a celebrity is a star

explanation.surface: A fan's first move is to keep embracing a famous person.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is used to introduce the first of several points, meaning initially.

clue.text: What may be hard to dry?

definitions.text: What may be hard to dry?

parts.words: What may be hard to dry?
parts.note: thick locks after a shower can take ages under the dryer

explanation.definitionFit: Thick tresses are notoriously slow to get dry with a towel or blower.

clue.text: Thoroughly impress dandy, reportedly, and live-in partner

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the dandy's word is spoken and heard as another

parts.note: a beau is a fashionable dandy
a lover can be a partner one lives with

explanation.surface: A fashionable man and his cohabiting partner make a big impression on everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAU is pronounced like BOW, the spelling the answer needs.
explanation.definitionFit: To bowl someone over is an idiom for overwhelming them with admiration or surprise.

clue.text: At university, superior by way of intelligence

parts.note: in British usage a student is up at university, i.e. in residence
top means best or superior

explanation.surface: A brilliant student at university rises above the rest through sheer brainpower.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British slang for in the head, referring to brains or mental capacity.

clue.text: A worker having eaten roll, departs full

parts.note: a bun is a bread roll
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A worker eats a bread roll and leaves feeling satisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plentiful exists in great quantity, so a supply is ample or overflowing.

clue.text: Wife sears fresh fish

indicators.note: fresh suggests the letters are made new, rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: A wife pan-fries a just-caught fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a family of brightly coloured reef species, including ballan types.

clue.text: Formal meeting in Bury to contend with

parts.note: to inter is to bury
to vie is to contend or compete

explanation.surface: Two parties meet formally in a Lancashire town to argue things out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the town but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A structured conversation, as for a job, is an official meeting with set questions.

clue.text: Italian river miles away from wood

indicators.note: away from means the distance letter is taken out of the wood word

parts.note: timber is wood

explanation.surface: An Italian river lies miles from any forest.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the river that flows through Rome.

clue.text: So sad, broadcast about English port

indicators.note: about means the scrambled letters go round the national abbreviation
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A gloomy radio programme is aired about an English harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' makes ODSSA from SO SAD, which goes around E.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Black Sea harbour city in Ukraine.

clue.text: Shorts all the rage? Nonsense

parts.note: something hot is fashionable, all the rage
pants is British slang for rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether short trousers are the latest fashion, then dismisses the idea.
explanation.definitionFit: These are very brief tight women's trousers, a type of short garment popular in the 1970s.

clue.text: Trying experience in old wood across river

indicators.note: across means the old wood spans the river, so the river letter sits inside

parts.note: deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: Crossing a river in an old wooden boat proves a gruelling business.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful or harrowing episode one must endure, a severe trial.

clue.text: Mocking father over in seedy bar

indicators.note: in means the turned word goes inside the bar

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable bar

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the father word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a father

explanation.surface: A father mocks someone in a run-down bar.

explanation.definitionFit: Scornful and jeering is the sense; both describe ridicule.

clue.text: Part of speech on one period of history is waffle

parts.note: a verb is a part of speech
I is the Roman numeral one
an age is a historical era

explanation.surface: A lecture about one era of history turns into rambling chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive wordiness, as in long-winded empty talk.

clue.text: Chess player's letters causing offence

parts.note: the player of the dark pieces in chess is Black
mail is letters delivered by post

explanation.surface: Letters from a chess player cause someone to take offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Extorting money with threats of exposure is a crime.

clue.text: The other woman may be married, I emphasise

parts.note: to stress is to emphasise

clue.text: Female injured diarist gets immediate treatment

indicators.note: injured means damaged, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman who keeps a journal gets hurt and is quickly patched up.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergency help given at the scene before a doctor arrives.

clue.text: Warning call about ancient city in uproar

indicators.note: about means the warning shout goes round the city

parts.note: golfers shout fore to warn of a ball in flight
Ur was an ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: A shouted warning about an old city causes a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A public outcry or angry stir is an uproar.

clue.text: Watchword of chap painting in retirement

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: in retirement means drawing back, so the word for painting is read backwards

parts.note: painting is a form of art

explanation.surface: A retired man's motto is to keep painting.

clue.text: A permit held by the runner

parts.note: taken as written
to let is to permit

clue.text: Rose playing ancient instrument in set

parts.note: the lute is an old stringed instrument

explanation.surface: Rose plays an old stringed instrument as part of a group.

clue.text: No mixer, single, introduced to both sides?

clue.text: Drawing of small sailing vessel

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A picture shows a little sailing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough quick picture is a type of drawing.

clue.text: Piece from Tahiti, a rare jewelled headdress

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An unusual piece of jewellery for the head comes from Tahiti.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara-style crown is a jewelled ornamental band worn on the head.

clue.text: Pole with no excess fat? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: spare means lean, with no excess fat

explanation.surface: A thin Polish person, nearly lean enough.

clue.text: Bird, yellow, heading off

parts.note: yellow means cowardly, craven

explanation.surface: A yellow bird flies off ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A large black corvid is a bird.

clue.text: Awfully pleased about a new walkway

indicators.note: about means the mixed-up letters go round the other two
awfully suggests the letters are badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is terribly delighted about a fresh seaside promenade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' makes ESPLADE from PLEASED, which goes 'about' A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafront promenade is a paved path for strolling.

clue.text: Statement to media and crowd regarding charter

parts.note: to press is to crowd; a press is a throng
re means regarding or about
to charter is to hire, as with a lease
